opportunity: A value a function returns in a float register printed as an integer or not at all, and a function that returns its callee's result (`call g; ret`) printed void while its callers read the result. clang -O0 `float qnan(void){return nanf("");}` printed `void sub_1150(void) { nanf((char *)0x2016); }` beside `v1 = (float)sub_1150();`, which no compiler accepts; a Cortex-M4F `nanf` printed `unsigned int sub_80049bc(void) { return 0x7fc00000; }` and its caller `(float)sub_80049bc()`, which evaluates to 2143289344.0 where the machine returns NaN. Over the 45 cast-corpus binaries main printed 2,123 uses of a void function's result.

analysis.type: p5_types/kuna_floatreg.rs votes a float of the register's width for a value a RETURN reads from a float-class output entry. It never votes a parameter: a function's callers decide what it receives, and a float parameter handed on or back printed a conversion by value in any caller or callee that holds the bits as an integer (x86-64 signbit_ handing its xmm0 float to f2u(unsigned int); Cortex-M4F/AArch64 putf2 moving s0 into r0 for put3(u32); a struct{float,float} caller; crazyflie O2-noinline sub_8028ae8 -> sub_8028914). The return vote is refused where the value's family holds an input, crosses a call (argument or result) that no declaration, protoorder statement or recorded recovery makes a float, is loaded through a pointer the function also moves integers through at that width, or where protoorder refuses a callee's float vote (integer computation, a store, a piece, a global); a NaN NAN cannot spell and one half of an ARM d register used whole also refuse. voidret (p4_calls/kuna_voidret.rs + decompile_all/callee_first.rs) redoes a function recovered void whose result a caller reads; a redo that leaves it returning a register a call only clobbers (an INDIRECT creation the call's output never replaced: gcc -O0 call_f2u, whose joined argument PIECE sits between the creation and the call) is withdrawn, and a float return any reader converts (held as an integer, passed to an integer parameter by position, stored through an integer pointer, returned as an integer) is withdrawn and its readers redone.
analysis.void: `call g; ret` is both `void f(){g();}` and `T f(){return g();}`; upstream's ancestorOpUse refuses a call's result outright and heritage registers no return trial for a register no op names. p4_calls/kuna_voidret.rs files, in decompile-all's callee-first run, every function recovered void and every call output a caller reads; the driver redoes such a function as soon as its first reader is decompiled, with the storage the callers read seeded, and accepts it only where it is the return value at every live RETURN (ancestorOpUse with a call's result counting), no wider than every path sets (set_tz returns eax, not a half-set rax). A later wider reader widens it; readers of different registers withdraw it.
analysis.readers: Every reader decompiled before a redo changed its callee's return is decompiled again (small readers always, readers over AUDIT_MAX_OPS only for a wrong value: an in-place offset from a now-scaled pointer, a float held as another type). A caller that refused or withdrew a callrettype statement of the other class converts explicitly ((long)sub_eecc(..)); a float statement is the token of a result held as raw bytes (a store through an untyped pointer stores the float).
analysis.libc: float/double added to the protos Ty vocabulary; the libcwiden corpus rule then admits ceil log2 modf pow sqrt strtod strtof; strtold (long double) and strtod_l (locale_t) stay rejected.
analysis.rejected_designs: Accepting the forced return wherever AncestorRealistic holds merged scratch-register values into the return variable (fmt get_space, sort xstrxfrm). Redoing every stale reader after the whole first pass cost bash -O2 +45% and sort -O2 +59% (their main functions redone, 10 s each); settling after each function redoes a wrapper at its first reader instead. Filtering stale readers by held class kept 112 conversions of stale results. An ARM pair rule that refused s0 whenever s1 was touched (every call's parameter trials touch it) left clampf an unsigned int returning fminf's float, a value conversion.

plan: Strict correctness fix, no option (a float register is the float declaration; a void function whose result a caller reads, and a caller whose text disagrees with its callee's declaration, are wrong output). Round trips compiled with gcc and clang that fail on main; stage test; corpus footprint classified with wrong-output counters; castbench, typesweep with arity counters, speed, all gates.

No parameter is typed float from its register: a function that only hands a float parameter on or back (idf, pass) keeps the integer its body gives it, and callers that pass it a computed float print the conversion main printed (clang -O0 call_f2u: v1 = f2u(dat_2004 + a0) beside f2u(unsigned int)); the parameter vote converted in whichever caller or callee held the bits as an integer instead

gcc -O0 call_f2u stays void: the PIECE that builds f2u's joined argument sits between the call and its INDIRECT creations, so the call never gains an output (collect_output_trial_varnodes looks only at the INDIRECTs right before the call); the redo that returned the clobbered register is withdrawn
Code that falls into fldz padding (openssh mprintf O2, scp O0 wrappers) returns 0.0 in ST0 where main printed an integer 0: the same bits, from a flow artifact main also had

gcc -O1/-O2 code that reads xmm0 after a call to a function returning a struct of two floats (`memcpy(&u, &v, 8); return u ^ i;`) gets no call output there (the whole-xmm0 ContainedBy gap above) and prints `sub_11b0(); return v1 ^ a0;` of an unset v1, as main does

A struct { float, float } getter (`return *p;`, movq (%rdi),%xmm0) whose caller reads only the low float returns `double` from `double *`, and the caller converts `(float)sub_11a0(..)` by value; main printed `unsigned long` and the same conversion

A getter that returns a global's float on one path and a constant on another stays an integer: every value returned in the register answers for the vote, and a global refuses it. crazyflie's packed-field getters (sub_80372d4, sub_8036c64) print unsigned int, and their readers print `(float)sub_80372d4()`, a value conversion, exactly as main does; the reviewed revision typed them float through the constant alone

A withdrawn function's float that comes from a callee's own float arithmetic or a declared (libc) return is not withdrawn: it is the type the machine computes, and a reader keeping it as an integer prints what main prints

Where every caller reads only the low 32 bits of a forced return and the callee kuna types as a pointer (tar O2 sub_26100 returning sub_412d0's int4 *, which returns futimens's int through a variable merged with __errno_location's pointer), the listing returns the pointer as unsigned int without a cast: a compile error under -Werror=int-conversion; the callers read only eax, so they get the bits the binary hands them. A return the callers read wider than the trial the function names is planted at their width (key_ssh_name returns char *), and refused where a path hands on a callee result wider or of unstated width that cannot be returned whole

A function whose callers read a 64-bit value in two registers stays `void`, as main prints it, when the model maps only one of them (`call big; ret` on i386 and ARM, dtotimespec's rax:rdx): its callers still read the result of a `void` function

gcc -O0 relocatable objects: a wrapper of a double callee prints `T v1; callee(..); return v1;` of an unset v1 on main and here (the call output is never linked); this branch types v1 double, and that function's per-function round trip loses the bits where main's `unsigned long` return left the callee's xmm0 in place by accident

Relocatable objects give a libc function no prototype, so a wrapper returning strtod's or strtof's result (and, on an image that does not state a hard-float convention, any named undeclared callee's) stays void, as main prints it, and its reader's `dat = parse();` still reads a void result. Linked binaries declare these calls

ARM images get no float/double libc rows. A soft-float or -mfloat-abi=softfp image hands a double around in r0:r1 and its callers hold that as a 64-bit integer: the rows made a function returning strtod's result or 0 `double`, which its readers converted by value, where main returns the right bits. A hard-float image's d0 is not among the default model's outputs: the rows made the same function `unsigned int` returning the low half of d0. strtod/pow/sqrt and their callers print as on main; an import stub whose callers read r0 returns that integer

An ARM hard-float wrapper of a double callee (`bl strtod; pop`) is planted at the d0 its caller reads, which the model's output map leaves out, so it stays void as main prints it (the previous head returned the s0 half)
On a soft-float image (u-boot O2), a wrapper whose callee kuna never decompiled (no body in the listing) stays void: its result could be a float in r0. 2 functions of 53,650 go back to main's text
